# Copilot instructions

## Architecture

This is a standalone ArcBox deployment project derived from Microsoft's Azure Arc Jumpstart. Code is MIT-licensed (`LICENSE-CODE`); other content retains `LICENSE`. Read `README.md` for deployment prerequisites and configuration.

`azure.yaml` selects the subscription-scoped `bicep\main.azd.bicep` wrapper, which creates `<environment-name>-rg` and delegates to the resource-group-scoped `bicep\main.bicep`. Management, client VM, and Kubernetes modules provision the infrastructure. `main.azd.parameters.json` maps azd environment variables to inputs. `hooks\common.ps1` implements prerequisite checks, environment persistence, and readiness polling for the lifecycle hooks.

The supported flavors are `ITPro` (nested Hyper-V servers), `DevOps` (Kubernetes/GitOps), and `DataOps` (Arc data services and disaster-recovery infrastructure). VM bootstrap runs under Windows PowerShell, persists machine environment variables, downloads artifacts, and schedules reboot/logon tasks. `WinGet.ps1` applies DSC YAML and starts flavor-specific logon scripts under PowerShell 7. Those scripts run the deployed-lab Pester checks.

## Build and test commands

Run from the repository root. Local hooks require PowerShell 7.3+; tests require Pester 5.6+.

```powershell
az bicep build --file .\bicep\main.azd.bicep
Invoke-Pester -Path .\hooks\tests -Output Detailed
Invoke-Pester -Path .\hooks\tests\azd.tests.ps1 -FullNameFilter '*accepts passing deployment checks*'
```

The hook suite mocks Azure CLI, azd, and SSH key generation. Windows-specific tests exercise the real Bootstrap parameter block with native `powershell.exe -File` binding without executing VM provisioning.

`hooks\tests\linux-onboarding.tests.py` requires Linux and Python 3 (no extra packages). Run it with Python under Linux/WSL to exercise real POSIX apt/dpkg lock contention and the actual onboarding shell entry point without installing packages or contacting Azure.

`hooks\tests\linux-sql-download.tests.py` also runs with Python under Linux/WSL. It exercises the Ubuntu SQL installer's real Bash download helper and entry point with isolated native commands, including DNS retries, deadline exhaustion, partial-file cleanup, and stopping before GPG/apt on a failed key download.

The same suite checks the standalone artifact URLs, generated ARM private-endpoint/DNS configuration, extension role-assignment dependencies, and fail-fast administrator secret retrieval. Network tests read the checked-in ARM, so regenerate affected templates before running them.

Bicep compilation reports compiler and linter diagnostics. Regenerate checked-in ARM from its matching Bicep entry point, for example:

```powershell
az bicep build --file .\bicep\main.bicep --outfile .\ARM\azuredeploy.json
az bicep build --file .\bicep\mgmt\mgmtArtifacts.bicep --outfile .\ARM\mgmt\mgmtArtifacts.json
```

`artifacts\tests` queries real Azure resources and the configured lab. Run those checks on the deployed client, not as local unit tests:

```powershell
& C:\ArcBox\Tests\Invoke-Test.ps1
Invoke-Pester -Path C:\ArcBox\Tests\common.tests.ps1 -FullNameFilter '*should have 30 resources or more*' -Output Detailed
```

The full VM runner updates wallpaper, tags, and scheduled tasks and can log off the session. `artifacts\integration_tests\scripts` supports transferring Pester XML from the client through staging storage.

For headless diagnostics on the client, invoke Pester directly against `common.tests.ps1` and the selected flavor suite with `-PassThru`; inspect `Result`, `TotalCount`, `PassedCount`, `FailedCount`, and failed-test errors. Do not run the full wallpaper/logoff runner under SYSTEM. Only publish readiness from an actual passing deployed run with a positive test count; never clear failure tags merely to unblock the waiter.

## Key conventions

- Templates download executable artifacts from `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/<githubAccount>/azd_arcbox/<githubBranch>/`, defaulting to `da5is` and `main`. Publish script changes before provisioning; local Bicep changes alone do not update downloaded VM scripts. `JS_GITHUB_USER` selects the external `jumpstart-apps` owner, not this automation repository. DevOps also uses `githubBranch` for sample applications, so that branch must exist there.
- Keep new inputs consistent across the azd wrapper, parameter mapping, main/child templates, extension command, Bootstrap parameter block, machine environment, consuming scripts, and README configuration table. Omit an empty optional `customLocationRPOID` from the native command line; DataOps requires the Custom Locations RP service-principal object ID.
- Bootstrap must remain Windows PowerShell-compatible; later scheduled tasks use `pwsh.exe`. Runtime paths are under `C:\ArcBox`, transcripts under `C:\ArcBox\Logs`, and variables such as `flavor`, `resourceGroup`, `subscriptionId`, and `templateBaseUrl` survive reboot at machine scope.
- Key Vault public network access is disabled. Its client-subnet private endpoint and `privatelink.vaultcore.azure.net` VNet link must exist before Bootstrap. DataOps domain-controller DNS forwards to `168.63.129.16`. Secret retrieval must fail explicitly, and an empty administrator password must not configure autologon.
- VM extensions depend on their required identity role assignments. VM scripts use managed identity and Key Vault; hooks use `Invoke-ArcBoxAz` for explicit subscription selection/native exit checking and `Set-ArcBoxEnvironmentValue` for azd/process persistence.
- Readiness is a tag protocol: the waiter accepts only `DeploymentProgress=Completed` and `DeploymentStatus=Tests succeeded: <positive integer> Tests failed: 0`. Preserve unrelated tags. ARM provisioning success alone is not readiness.
- Each azd environment owns its entire resource group. Existing labs cannot change flavor or adopt unrelated groups. Cluster suffixes are deterministic per subscription/environment. Retained `.azure` data contains generated credentials and SSH keys needed for retries. `azd down` deletes the entire group; interrupting the readiness wait does not delete resources.
- VM profiles provide `Write-Header` and `exec`. Bootstrap installs `Azure.Arc.Jumpstart.Common` from PowerShell Gallery, so editing its repository source alone does not update the installed module.
- Preprovision prompts once for `JS_ARCBOX_PASSWORD` with hidden confirmation; it is stored in the ignored `.azure/<environment>/.env` file in plaintext for retries. Pass the same secret as both secure Bicep parameters and store it in Key Vault. The prebuilt Windows guest images ship with a bootstrap Administrator password that setup must use only to rotate each local account to the shared password; all subsequent remote access and deployed checks use the Key Vault value.
- The first shared-password deployment failed during prebuilt SQL guest setup because the password-rotation remoting session did not load `Microsoft.SqlServer.Management.Smo.Server`. Import `SqlServer` with terminating error handling inside that session before constructing the SMO server; importing it in the separate `prepareSqlServerForAssessment.ps1` child process does not load assemblies into later remoting sessions. Local regression tests cover the session import and failures; the later successful ITPro deployment also passed this setup stage.
- ITPro has six nested guests: `win22sql22` (the prebuilt SQL Server 2022 VM), `win16sql16` (Windows Server 2016 Datacenter Evaluation with SQL Server 2016 SP3), `win19sql19` (Windows Server 2019 with SQL Server 2019), `win25sql25` (Windows Server 2025 with SQL Server 2025), `ubu24sql25` (Ubuntu 24.04 with SQL Server 2025), and `ubu24` (Ubuntu 24.04 without SQL or SQL-specific extensions). Windows SQL samples retain FILESTREAM ArchiveDB; Linux has AdventureWorksLT2025 and the same ArchiveDB Records columns with ordinary VARBINARY(MAX), since FILESTREAM is unsupported on Linux. Keep runtime names consistent across Hyper-V/hostnames/Arc; original Ubuntu source VHD names remain unchanged. Do not select the renamed guests with `Get-VM *Ubuntu*`. `JS_SQL_SERVER_EDITION` affects only `win22sql22`.
- The published image feed has no Windows Server 2016 disk. `ArcBoxWindows2016.ps1` builds a 60-GB dynamic UEFI/GPT disk from Microsoft's official Datacenter Evaluation Desktop Experience ISO on the client, protects the runtime answer file containing the shared password, waits for first boot, removes answer files, and installs signed .NET Framework 4.8 before SQL/Arc. Windows evaluation activation is restricted to `win16sql16`/build 14393 and requires an activated, unexpired TIMEBASED_EVAL license; other Windows guests retain KMS validation. This 180-day OS evaluation is independent of the SQL installation mode. Use a new environment rather than converting old guest disks/names. Local regressions are not deployed image-build/extension proof; the earlier all-green deployment used the previous Windows OS pairings.
- `JS_NESTED_SQL_MODE` selects only Developer (direct-template default) or Evaluation for SQL 2016/2019/2025. Evaluation can be manually converted to licensed Standard/Enterprise using version-matched licensed media; verify the actual edition/version, then configure Arc's License with Software Assurance (`Paid`, not PAYG) manually if entitled. Setup creates new extensions with `LicenseOnly`, preserves existing extension licensing/settings, and accepts converted Standard/Enterprise instances on Evaluation retries without inferring SA. Edition conversion and ESU enrollment remain manual. The former BYOL installation mode/edition input and `Installation.json` license-reconciliation protocol were removed; old BYOL environments must select Evaluation. Evaluation media is cached separately from Developer, and SQL 2016 Evaluation setup integrates SP3. Local mocked coverage is not proof of a deployed Evaluation installation or licensed conversion.
- The ITPro preprovision hook prompts for missing `JS_NESTED_SQL_MODE` using dev/eval (or numbers/full names), then persists the canonical mode only after ownership/flavor checks. Explicit settings skip the menu; unattended ITPro requires a configured mode. DevOps/DataOps do not prompt for it. Enter/Q cancels before Azure operations. Developer remains the direct-template default, not an implicit choice in the hook.
- A deployed Evaluation selection installed Developer because local Bicep passed Evaluation while `githubBranch=main` downloaded older Developer-only scripts and checks. Evaluation preprovision now requires published Bootstrap/logon/installer/ITPro checks to match the checkout (CRLF/LF ignored) before Azure operations. Select the published artifact branch explicitly; local Git branch selection does not change it. A passing preflight is not a deployed Evaluation installation. Correcting the source does not convert existing guests; do not rerun Bootstrap's initial disk setup as recovery.
- ESU enrollment remains manual and potentially billable. Evaluation is a 180-day trial, not a production ESU entitlement. Standard/Enterprise production ESUs require qualifying SA/subscription or PAYG. Microsoft also documents Developer-edition ESUs for qualifying nonproduction environments associated with production ESU subscriptions; do not restore the blanket claim that Developer must always be converted before ESU enrollment.
- Budget ITPro guest memory against the client SKU: the prebuilt SQL guest uses 6 GB, the three other Windows guests use 4 GB each, `ubu24sql25` uses 4 GB with a 2048-MB SQL limit, and `ubu24` uses 2 GB (24 GB total). The previous two 4-GB Ubuntu defaults caused a startup failure on the 32-GB `Standard_D8s_v5` client. The successful 56-check ITPro deployment includes concurrent SQL-query host-headroom validation; this is not a sizing guarantee for other SKUs or workloads.
- ITPro's new Arc-only baseline assignments use stable built-ins with IncludeArcMachines=true and AuditIfNotExists, not deny/remediation or the old preview initiative. Machine Configuration runs inside the Arc agent. Do not harden lab settings merely to make audit reports compliant; missing reports are not proof of compliance.
- ITPro adds an Azure Monitor workspace for native AMA OTel metrics while retaining Log Analytics and existing SQL/classic-monitoring DCRs. AMA and ChangeTracking-Windows/Linux plus DCR associations are explicitly ensured on all six guests after onboarding. The WindowsOpenSSH Arc extension applies only to Windows; Ubuntu uses native SSH. Arc SSH configuration uses PowerShell REST payloads to avoid az.cmd JSON quote loss. The successful 56-check ITPro deployment validated actual telemetry and SSH from all six guests, not just extension provisioning.
- SQL Server 2025 on Ubuntu 24.04 requires CU1 or later. The Linux install maps Developer to MSSQL_PID=EnterpriseDeveloper (not the older Developer value), passes the shared secret over stdin/environment rather than command arguments, discovers backup logical filenames with RESTORE FILELISTONLY, and reuses databases on retries. JS_NESTED_SQL_MODE also controls this Linux instance; do not change existing extension licensing on retries.
- Server management validation checks new ConfigurationChange records using a unique temporary service name, fresh per-resource OTel samples, and actual inventory/logs. Queries use the Azure Monitor workspace endpoint with Monitoring Data Reader scoped to that workspace. Native OTel names/resource labels may contain dots; query with PromQL UTF-8 syntax, not assumptions about legacy underscore labels. Baseline NonCompliant is a valid evaluated audit result, not automatic remediation authority.
- Bootstrap explicitly installs Az.OperationalInsights for ITPro's workspace and ingestion checks; do not assume Az.Accounts, Az.Resources, or the common Gallery module supplies those query commands.
- A fresh workspace rejected the inventory DCR with InvalidOutputTable despite successful ARM validation. Creating the built-in ConfigurationChange/ConfigurationData tables first also failed with SolutionNotActive until the workspace's OMSGallery/ChangeTracking solution was active. Deploy that solution, then the tables, then the DCR with explicit dependencies; this prerequisite was verified by actual infrastructure deployment before any client VM was created. This does not deploy an Automation account/MMA agent or prove guest telemetry/clean-lab success.
- The first clean setup attempt stopped on win22sql22 KMS contact error 0xC004F074; a later read-only check found TCP 1688 reachable and an activated VOLUME_KMSCLIENT license without manual activation. Activate only after guest network initialization/rename, retry that transient contact error with a bound, and still require the actual CIM license state. Do not infer that installing a KMS key alone means activation succeeded.
- A recovered setup's first authorized_keys directory copy to ubu24 returned Hyper-V 0x80004005 even with the correct directory destination; the exact same copy succeeded later without a guest restart or path change. Copy-ArcBoxLinuxGuestFile bounds retries of that specific observed startup error and surfaces other/persistent failures. Heartbeat/healthy integration status is not sufficient file-copy evidence; keep the directory-destination convention.
- Linux systemctl enable emitted informational stderr ("Synchronizing state...") that became a terminating remote error under the host's ErrorActionPreference=Stop despite native success. Capture/merge native stderr inside the Linux remoting block and inspect LASTEXITCODE; stream installer/onboarding output as text rather than forwarding native ErrorRecord objects. Do not globally relax error handling or ignore failing exit codes.
- Linux onboarding connected both guests but then returned 127: the downloaded template had zero CR bytes while Windows Set-Content appended one CR to the generated script. Normalize to LF and use -NoNewline when substituting the runtime token, then test the actual generated bytes. Do not publish that secret-substituted file. Preserve the hostname in Linux Arc resource naming rather than title-casing it; the old sed transform produced Ubu24/Ubu24sql25 despite the requested lowercase names.
- PowerShell variable names are case-insensitive: the former additional-SQL foreach iterator `$sqlVmName` overwrote the prebuilt guest's `$SQLvmName`, duplicating win25sql25 and excluding win22sql22 from later management/SSH. Use a distinct iterator, reject duplicate target lists, and test the actual caller's variable flow rather than only calling the helper with six correct literals.
- An evaluated AuditIfNotExists policy can be NonCompliant because the guest assignment is missing, not because OS settings were evaluated. Ensure missing AzureWindowsBaseline/AzureLinuxBaseline guest assignments explicitly with assignmentType=Audit, using the built-in definition's own guestConfiguration metadata/default parameters. This was accepted for a missing Windows assignment through the scoped ARM API; preserve existing assignments and never switch to an applying mode.
- The Guest Configuration collection omitted an explicit baseline assignment even after its direct GET returned a real NonCompliant report. Use the direct per-machine AzureWindowsBaseline/AzureLinuxBaseline resource for existence and report checks, not the incomplete collection. Handle only 404 as absent; authorization/API failures must remain errors.
- Native OTel exact-name queries returned real samples for all six guests, while the metric-name wildcard selector returned HTTP 501. Use quoted native metric names in PromQL. On this SQL 2025 Linux build, mssql-conf get memory.memorylimitmb returned exit 0 with "No setting" despite the configuration containing 2048; verify the exact persisted memory value through the INI parser instead.
- Windows Server 2025 had a running/listening sshd but only a Private-profile OpenSSH firewall rule, and SSH from the host timed out. Ensure an Any-profile guest rule restricted to the internal 10.10.1.0/24 lab subnet; do not change the network category, disable the firewall, or open public Azure SSH ports.
- ARM JSON with `metadata._generator.name=bicep` is generated; parameter, Kubernetes, and workbook JSON are not. `.gitattributes` requires LF for shell files. Never publish `.azure`, logs, private keys, runtime kubeconfigs, or secret-substituted copies of templates. Shared-storage SAS telemetry was removed; do not reintroduce its credential or upstream queue reporting.

## Deployment and troubleshooting

Use the selected environment explicitly and authenticate azd and Azure CLI to the same tenant. For unattended provisioning, configure `JS_ARCBOX_FLAVOR` and, for ITPro, `JS_NESTED_SQL_MODE`, set `AZD_NO_PROMPT=true`, and run `azd up --environment <environment-name> --no-prompt`; the CLI flag alone does not disable prompts in custom hooks.

ITPro has been deployed successfully in `swedencentral` with zone `1`, the client public IP, and private Key Vault connectivity. This does not validate DevOps/DataOps or every VM SKU in that region; check quota and service availability for the selected flavor.

Earlier recovered-lab validation passed 56 deployed checks and 219 local regressions; those results alone did not establish clean-deployment success. After the subsequent provisioning fixes through commit `e0e08fc`, the user reported an all-green ITPro deployment on October 22, 2026. The agent independently read resource-group readiness tags confirming `DeploymentProgress=Completed` and `DeploymentStatus=Tests succeeded: 56 Tests failed: 0`. The user reconfirmed everything looked good on October 26. This establishes successful end-to-end ITPro readiness, including final test-result/wallpaper publication, rather than ARM provisioning alone. The checks cover all six guests' inventory/change records, OTel CPU/memory/disk/network metrics, SSH, evaluated audit reports, Windows activation, SQL samples/editions, the Linux SQL memory cap, and concurrent SQL-query host headroom. Local validation for `e0e08fc` passed 274 PowerShell and 12 Linux tests. Do not infer that every transient-error recovery branch fired, that no manual intervention occurred, or that other flavors/SKUs/regions were validated. Licensed edition conversion and ESU enrollment remain unverified.

The readiness wait starts after infrastructure provisioning and defaults to 360 minutes. Query the resource-group tags without retrieving secure deployment parameters:

```powershell
az group show --subscription <subscription-id> --name <environment-name>-rg --query '{progress:tags.DeploymentProgress,status:tags.DeploymentStatus}' --output json
```

For ITPro, expected stages include Bootstrap, `Restarting and installing WinGet packages...`, `Installing WinGet packages...`, `Downloading and configuring nested SQL VM`, `Downloading and configuring nested VMs`, then `Completed`. A stage can contain large VHDX downloads, Hyper-V creation, guest reboots, and Arc onboarding. Unchanged tags alone do not establish a hang; compare transcript timestamps, worker processes, and nested VM state.

- At the reboot/WinGet boundary, inspect `WinGetLogonScript` and `Get-ScheduledTaskInfo`, interactive sessions, and `C:\ArcBox\Logs\WinGet-provisioning-*.log`. Result `267011` (`0x41303`) means the task has never run; `267009` (`0x41301`) means it is running.
- If autologon never started, check only whether `DefaultPassword` is present, not its value. Bootstrap retrieves that password from Key Vault; `ForbiddenByConnection` with public access disabled and no private endpoint is a vault network problem, not a bad supplied administrator password. Verify the endpoint, DNS zone group, VNet link, and managed-identity roles. Role assignment creation and DNS configuration do not guarantee instantaneous propagation.
- A subnet with `defaultOutboundAccess=false` and no NAT gateway is expected for ITPro without Bastion: the client's attached public IP supplies explicit outbound connectivity. Verify NIC association and HTTPS reachability before adding NAT. Public internet connectivity does not grant access to the private Key Vault.
- Autologon is intentionally temporary. `ArcServersLogonScript.ps1` and `DevOpsLogonScript.ps1` remove its registry values after starting. Missing values later in setup are not a regression. A policy-enforced logon notice can interfere with autologon; do not remove that policy as a troubleshooting shortcut.
- Inspect `C:\ArcBox\Logs\ArcServersLogonScript.log` and `Get-VM` on the client for ITPro nested-VM stages. VHDX files are under `F:\Virtual Machines`. Avoid returning whole transcripts: they can contain tokens, credentials, or secret-substituted command lines.
- A confirmed hang at `Downloading and configuring nested VMs` occurred with Ubuntu-02 powered off: Hyper-V Worker events 3122/3050 reported insufficient memory, while setup waited indefinitely at `Get-VM *Ubuntu* | Wait-VM -For Heartbeat`. Check VM state, heartbeat integration services, host free memory, and Hyper-V Worker/Admin events before retrying downloads or extending the timeout. Reducing Ubuntu startup memory to 2 GB and starting the guests resumed the existing setup process.
- SQL extension settings must use a JSON file passed as `--settings @<path>`: inline unescaped JSON loses double quotes through Windows `az.cmd`, which broke even the original SQL VM after the additional-version changes. `Install-ArcBoxSqlExtension` checks native exit codes and extension provisioning state with a 15-minute timeout. Query extensions directly; do not infer extension readiness from the parent machine's `Resource` collection or a null `StatusCode`.
- Additional SQL installations publish per-version progress tags. HTTP downloads and installer processes have 60-minute limits, failed HTTP downloads are cleaned up, and database restores have a 30-minute timeout. Setup arguments containing paths must be quoted for `Start-Process`. A progress tag identifies the last published stage, not necessarily the failing command; the SQL 2025 tag remained visible during later onboarding and policy-scan work.
- After asynchronous SQL extension creation, an immediate `show` returned exit code 3 even though the extension subsequently succeeded. Poll the ARM extension collection described below: an empty successful response means not yet visible, not failure. Reuse successful extensions and connected Windows agents on retries. Top-level terminating failures publish `DeploymentProgress=Failed` without exposing error text in tags.
- A later clean setup stopped when its unconditional AzureMonitorWindowsAgent create overlapped an existing installation: ARM returned HCRP409 at the first SQL guest's monitoring step, and the original operation subsequently succeeded. The prebuilt SQL guest now uses Install-ArcBoxServerExtension to reuse successful/pending AMA installations and bound status polling. Only HCRP409 with a matching publisher and healthy/pending extension is recoverable; unrelated native errors remain fatal. Allow delayed collection visibility within the original 20-minute deadline. Bootstrap downloads this helper for both ITPro and DataOps. The later successful ITPro deployment passed this stage; local regressions cover delayed visibility without claiming the live conflict branch fired.
- The Windows SQL extension can also race another installation: a fresh run failed creating WindowsAgent.SqlServer on win19sql16 with HCRP409, while that extension subsequently succeeded. Install-ArcBoxSqlExtension now recovers only HCRP409 after verifying the matching Microsoft.AzureData publisher/type and pending/success state. Allow delayed collection visibility within the original 15-minute deadline; never recreate the extension or overwrite licensing/ESU settings to resolve the conflict. Local regressions cover real native stderr, pending-to-success/failure transitions, and the shared visibility/completion deadline. The later successful ITPro deployment passed SQL extension setup, but does not prove the live conflict branch fired.
- A subsequent clean setup reached management configuration but ChangeTracking-Linux 2.42 failed because cxp.service and its collector package were absent after the handler's install returned. Re-running the downloaded Microsoft handler's install/enable restored the package and an active/enabled service; the same version installed successfully on the other Ubuntu guest. The underlying reason for the first omitted package installation is unconfirmed; do not assert an apt lock or version regression. Setup retries that exact missing-unit failure once through the existing guest SSH session, checks native exit codes and the actual service, and waits within the extension deadline for ARM success. It preserves extension settings and fails on unrelated errors. This targeted recovery is not clean end-to-end deployment proof.
- Another run completed Windows SQL 2025 but failed during Linux Arc-agent installation because unattended-upgrades held the apt/dpkg frontend lock beyond Microsoft's short installer wait. The Ubuntu onboarding script now waits up to 30 minutes for actual POSIX package locks and retries only the vendor's exact lock-busy error within that original deadline. Never remove lock files, kill package-manager processes, or disable security updates to bypass contention. The caller publishes a separate Ubuntu onboarding progress stage. Local Linux lock/installer tests are not clean-deployment proof; this does not establish that apt contention caused the earlier Change Tracking missing-service failure.
- A later fresh run passed all 56 deployed checks but failed before publishing readiness because bginfo.exe was absent. WinGet had rejected the rolling BGInfo.zip download with hash mismatch 0x8a150011, and WinGet.ps1 ignored the failed common configuration. BGInfo now installs from Microsoft's official ZIP only after validating the executable's Microsoft Corporation Authenticode signature, to C:\ArcBox\Tools\Bginfo64.exe; do not bypass WinGet hash validation. The runner uses that explicit path and checks process exit. WinGet configuration errors must publish Failed, retain the recovery task, and prevent launching flavor setup. The later successful ITPro deployment reached final wallpaper/readiness publication. BGInfo is inherited desktop test-result display tooling, not a newly added monitoring agent or Azure service.
- A subsequent run failed before Change Tracking while downloading Ubuntu SQL's signing key: curl exited 6 resolving packages.microsoft.com, then GPG failed on empty input. Later DNS/HTTPS probes succeeded on both guests. ITPro DHCP incorrectly advertised the DataOps-only 10.16.2.100 resolver alongside Azure DNS; advertise only 168.63.129.16 for ITPro, preserving DataOps configuration. This invalid fallback was observed as the SQL guest's current resolver, but is not proven to have caused the exact failed lookup. SQL metadata downloads now retry only transient network failures within each original five-minute budget, stage complete files, and never invoke GPG after a failed key download. The exact helper recovered an injected DNS failure and downloaded the real key on the deployed guest; local regressions cover persistent failures. The subsequent successful ITPro deployment completed Ubuntu SQL setup and final readiness, without establishing that a natural DNS retry occurred during that run.
- SQL setup exit 3010 writes a per-version `RestartRequired` marker; the Hyper-V host restarts the guest, waits for PowerShell Direct, clears the marker, and reruns database provisioning. Timed-out setup terminates the installer PID tree; SQL module installation is bounded to 15 minutes. VM-side recovery must run in the scheduled task's user/profile context, after verifying no other worker is active.
- Check AzCopy and WinGet configuration exit codes before using downloaded disks or guests. On the deployed client, changing `AutomaticStopAction` from `Save` to `ShutDown` on a running guest fails with Hyper-V `0x80041001`; changing `AutomaticStartAction` works online. `Set-ArcBoxGuestLifecycle` gracefully shuts down only guests needing the stop-policy change, waits up to 180 seconds without forcing power off, and restores their original running state even if the settings update fails. Already configured guests are not interrupted on retries. Merge the `ArcSQLServerExtensionDeployment=Disabled` tag with `az tag update --operation Merge`, never replace the group's ownership/readiness tags.
- `Save-ArcBoxGuestDisk` downloads only missing disks through staging files, checks attached disk paths, and publishes completed downloads without overwriting existing disks. Linux onboarding uses `set -eu`, reuses an agent connected to the requested subscription/group, and checks installer/connect failures. Its generated script substitutes values inside existing double quotes; do not add literal single quotes to those replacements.
- SQL extension polling now uses `az rest` against the ARM extension collection with API `2024-07-10`, selecting `value[].properties.provisioningState`. The connectedmachine CLI list query returned an empty state for a deployed successful extension; do not rely on its version-dependent output flattening.
- Linux `Copy-VMFile` destinations must be directories, not filenames: the deployed `hv_fcopy_daemon` appends the source basename. Use `/home/jumpstart/.ssh` for source `authorized_keys` and `/home/jumpstart` for the onboarding script. A filename destination produced `authorized_keys/authorized_keys`, guest journal `Open Failed: Not a directory`, and host error `0x80004005` despite healthy integration-service status.
- Ubuntu heartbeat and IP waits have 10-minute limits, but healthy Hyper-V integration status does not prove file-copy success. Inspect the guest's `hv-fcopy-daemon.service` journal for the actual target path and error. The corrected directory destinations were verified by successful copies and key-authenticated SSH on both deployed Ubuntu guests.
- Separate ArchiveDB creation, its FILESTREAM table creation, and recovery-mode configuration with `GO` in the `Invoke-Sqlcmd` query. SQL Server 2016 compiled the cross-database `CREATE TABLE` before executing `CREATE DATABASE` in a single batch, failing with error 2702 (`Database 'ArchiveDB' does not exist`) even though engine installation and AdventureWorks restore succeeded.
- A deployed run completed all three added SQL installations and Arc onboarding, then stopped at the missing `Start-AzPolicyComplianceScan` command before Pester. Even with `Az.PolicyInsights` installed, that cmdlet polls subscription-scoped `asyncOperationResults`, which the resource-group-scoped client identity cannot read. Submit the resource-group policy scan using `Invoke-AzRestMethod` and check HTTP acceptance; do not widen identity permissions for subscription-level polling. Submission is asynchronous, not proof of policy compliance. Retain the setup task until final validation has run, rather than unregistering it before the policy scan.

For remote inspection, use Azure VM Run Command with a bounded diagnostic script passed as `--scripts @<script-file>` rather than embedding multiline PowerShell in a native command string. Check both stdout and stderr; a successful Run Command invocation is not proof that every guest command succeeded.

Check the client power state before Run Command. A deallocated client cannot execute diagnostics; obtain approval before starting it because compute charges resume. Run Command executes as SYSTEM under Windows PowerShell by default, not as the provisioning user under PowerShell 7. Use `pwsh.exe` explicitly for PowerShell 7 diagnostics. A SYSTEM OpenSSH private-key ACL error does not prove the provisioning user's key is unusable; verify authentication in the appropriate context without weakening key permissions.

An interrupted or timed-out wait leaves Azure resources running. Resume the waiter without reprovisioning using `azd hooks run postprovision --environment <environment-name>`. This does not restart a failed VM setup worker, and pulling repository changes does not update scripts already downloaded onto the client. For worker recovery, diagnose the terminating error, publish and install the corrected artifacts, verify no existing worker is active, then restart the setup task in its intended user/profile context. If recreation is requested, `azd down --environment <environment-name> --purge` removes the entire group and purges the soft-deleted vault. Retain the private, ignored `.azure` configuration rather than regenerating credentials for an existing environment.

## Maintaining these instructions

After future implementation or deployment investigations, update directly relevant lessons here with verified behavior and validation scope. Replace superseded guidance instead of appending contradictory bullets. Distinguish local regression tests, recovered-lab checks, and clean end-to-end deployments; do not turn suspected causes into established facts. Keep reusable operational guidance, not private environment identifiers, credentials, full transcripts, or one-off diagnostic commands. Commit instruction changes with the related fix and publish them when requested so future deployments use the recorded lessons.
